33.       {:ok, "<!doctype html><html xmlns=..."}
34.

1. defmodule Mjml do
2.   @moduledoc """
3.   Provides functions for transpiling MJML email templates to HTML.
4.   """
5. 
6.   @doc """
7.   Converts an MJML string to HTML content.
8. 
9.   Returns a result tuple:
10. 
11.   * `{:ok, html}` for a successful MJML transpiling
12.   * `{:error, message}` for a failed MJML transpiling
13. 
14.   You can pass render options to customize the rendering of the final HTML:
15. 
16.   * `keep_comments` – when `false`, removes the comments from the rendered HTML.
17.     Defaults to `true`.
18. 
19.   * `social_icon_path` – when given, uses this base path to generate social icon URLs.
20.     E.g. `social_icon_path: "https://example.com/icons/"` will generate a social icon
21.     URL, like "https://example.com/icons/github.png"
22. 
23.   ## Examples
24. 
25.       iex> Mjml.to_html("<mjml><mj-head></mj-head></mjml>")
26.       {:ok, "<!doctype html><html xmlns=..."}
27. 
28.       iex> Mjml.to_html("something not MJML")
29.       {:error, "Couldn't convert MJML template"}
30. 
31.       iex> opts = [keep_comments: false, social_icon_path: "https://example.com/icons/"]
32.       iex> Mjml.to_html("<mjml><mj-head></mj-head></mjml>", opts)
33.       {:ok, "<!doctype html><html xmlns=..."}
34. 
35.   """
36.   def to_html(mjml, opts \\ []) do
37.     options = struct(Mjml.RenderOptions, opts)
38.     Mjml.Native.to_html(mjml, options)
39.   end
40. end

Implemented the MRML compatibility fix in `native/mjml_nif/src/lib.rs`.
